research.summary:
SMR publishing is a manual, web-first flow. Sign in with GitHub/Google/Facebook, create the mod page (auto-approved; mod_reference is immutable, 3-32 chars), then edit it to set the mandatory AI-use and network-use disclosures, then upload Alpakit's multi-target YourModReference.zip. Pak-only versions auto-approve; any .dll/.so is scanned on VirusTotal (auto-approved if malicious<=1 and suspicious<=1). Limits: 4 new mods per user and 5 versions per mod per 24 h; a version name can never be reused.

Decision-driving findings:
1. This Claude-built mod must declare ai_usage with a written description. That is normal on SMR (378 of the top 1000 mods disclose AI use, including Smart!).
2. SMR rejects a descriptor whose Version differs from the SemVersion major. The owner's CompanionPresence.uplugin (Version 5, SemVersion 0.4.1, exact pins) must not be the template.
3. RequiredOnRemote defaults to true and SML checks on both sides. Docs say exact versions; code defaults to ">= own version"; the combined effect is lockstep versions. A mismatch disconnects with "Client/Server missing mods".
4. SML is GPL-3.0 with no linking exception. The FSF treats dynamically linked plug-ins as one combined program, so license the mod GPL-compatibly (GPL-3.0-or-later, MIT or Apache-2.0) and publish source.
5. FactoryGame headers are (c) Coffee Stain: never vendor them or game assets.
6. The SMR ToS forbids links to off-site mod binaries and use of the API in closed-source apps.

Install: SMM and ficsit-cli manage servers over SFTP/SMB. Manual copy into FactoryGame/Mods/<ModRef> is unsupported. The wolveix image has no SFTP; SKIPUPDATE=true pins the game build.

Automation: `ficsit smr upload <mod-id>` works with the login session token. How to obtain it is undocumented; api.ficsit.dev is an unofficial staging instance.

Policy: I found no Coffee Stain EULA, fan-content or trademark policy (the Steam EULA page failed to load), only community guidelines. "Satisfactory" and "FICSIT" appear in many mod names; add an unaffiliated disclaimer.

Docs hosting: SMR sanitized Markdown, GitHub Pages, docs.ficsit.app by request.

claims.statement: SMR refuses every version upload until the mod page carries an AI-use disclosure. The content policy requires disclosure when portions of source code were directly created by generative AI. Because this mod is Claude-built, the disclosure must be type ai_usage with a written description.

The network-use disclosure is also required before upload, and an empty string appears to mean 'no network use' (stored as null/empty/non-empty). A disclosure, once set, cannot be cleared. Mods must state any external network connectivity, except multiplayer and game-to-game synchronization.

claims.statement: RequiredOnRemote defaults to true. SML runs the mod-list check on both sides: the server validates clients (IsServer=true) and, since SML 3.9.0, the client validates the server (IsServer=false). A mod with RequiredOnRemote true that the other side lacks, or whose version fails the range, closes the connection with '<Client|Server> missing mods: ...'. Docs say the default RemoteVersionRange is exact-version. Code defaults it to '>= own SemVersion'. Because each side requires the other to be >= itself, the effective result is lockstep versions: a 1.0.0 server rejects a 1.1.0 client. The check can be skipped with the console variable SML.SkipRemoteModListCheck. RequiredOnRemote=false makes a mod server-only or client-only without error.

claims.statement: SML is licensed GPL-3.0 (plain GPLv3 text; no linking exception text found; no per-file headers found). The FSF's published position is that a dynamically linked plug-in that calls the main program is one combined program and must be licensed under the GPL or a GPL-compatible licence, with source. A more permissive GPL-compatible licence is allowed (MIT/Expat; Apache-2.0 with GPLv3). Mods in the wild vary (FicsIt-Networks GPL-3.0; FRM and Circuitry show no licence). Whether a given mod is a derivative work is a legal question that no court has settled for SML. This is the FSF's interpretation, not legal advice.

evidence.quote: GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007

If the main program dynamically links plug-ins, and they make function calls to each other and share data structures, we believe they form a single combined program, which must be treated as an extension of both the main program and the plug-ins.

If the main program and the plugins are a single combined program then this means you must license the plug-in under the GPL or a GPL-compatible free software license and distribute it with source code in a GPL-compliant way.
You can, if you wish, release your module under a license which is more lax than the GPL but compatible with the GPL.
This is a lax, permissive non-copyleft free software license, compatible with the GNU GPL.
This is a free software license, compatible with version 3 of the GNU GPL.

verdicts.note: All 3 quotes verified verbatim at the pinned commits; smr-api pin f1f39d09 is current main HEAD; smr-frontend main differs from the pin only by a typo fix in content-policy. CreateVersion returns 'you must provide an AI use disclosure before uploading a version' when ai_use_disclosure is nil, and a second error if the type is not no_ai_usage and the message is empty. Enum (schemas/mod.graphql): no_ai_usage | ai_usage | runtime_ai_usage. ai_usage is the right type by elimination (runtime_ai_usage is for runtime generative AI, and the policy lists source code created by generative AI as disclosable). Omitted by the claim: CreateVersion ALSO refuses upload without network_use_disclosure (nil check at the next lines). UpdateMod forbids clearing an AI disclosure once set. createMod itself works without a disclosure (tests/ai_use_disclosure_test.go); only version upload is gated. Live ficsit.app pages are SPA shells, so evidence is repo source, not rendered pages.

verdicts.corrected: The mod_reference is effectively permanent: docs say it cannot be changed once the SMR page exists, and UpdateMod returns 'this mod already has set a mod reference' unless the mod ID equals its reference. It must match the plugin folder and C++ Source folder. The SMR frontend form enforces ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ and 3-32 chars; the backend NewMod has no validate tag on mod_reference and the DB schema only sets MaxLen(32), so the regex and the minimum are frontend-only. The backend blocklist (satisfactory, factorygame, sml, satisfactorymodloader, examplemod, docmod, gamefeatures) is a whole-string match on strings.ToLower(), so case-insensitive. CreateMod also rejects a reference equal to an existing mod ID. On 2026-10-13 a GET to api.ficsit.app getModByReference returned 'mod not found' for Redstone, Signal, Logic, Wiring and FicsitRedstone, but that only shows nothing visible holds them: Mod uses SoftDeleteMixin with a plain unique index on mod_reference, so a soft-deleted mod could still block creation. Availability is proven only when CreateMod succeeds.

Verified: 'SemVer major version should match Version' (validateUPluginJSON, upload runs with withValidation=true), static/uplugin-json-schema.json requires FileVersion, Version and GameVersion, and the SemVersion pattern is strict. ReleaseMod.adoc quotes on 1.0.0, avoiding major 0, '>=something' GameVersion and the ^ prefix are verbatim. CompanionPresence.uplugin at ee830e84 (and the local copy) has Version 5 / SemVersion 0.4.1, so split[0]='0' != '5' and SMR rejects it. Nuances: (1) the Version/SemVersion mismatch is the only hard rejection; GameVersion '502094.0.0' and an exact SML '3.12.0' pass the schema and are only fragile or against the docs' advice. (2) SemVersion is not in the schema's required list; if absent SMR synthesizes 'Version.0.0' (docs call it required). (3) The cited CompanionPresence quote is three adjacent lines joined with spaces, not one contiguous line.

verdicts.corrected: Core is right: RequiredOnRemote defaults to true; both sides run ValidateSMLConnectionData (server with IsServer=true, client via HandleWelcomePlayer_Client with false; docs: 'The reverse (client checking host) is implemented as of SML 3.9.0'); the default RemoteVersionRange in code is '>= own SemVersion' while the docs say exact; and SML.SkipRemoteModListCheck skips the check. The effective result is lockstep versions. But the example is backwards: with a 1.0.0 server and a 1.1.0 client, the server accepts (1.1.0 matches >=1.0.0) and the CLIENT closes the connection, because the server's 1.0.0 fails its >=1.1.0 range, showing 'Server missing mods: ... required: >=1.1.0, server: 1.0.0'. Conversely a 1.1.0 server rejects a 1.0.0 client. RequiredOnRemote=false only skips the branch where the remote lacks the mod; if both sides have the mod and the version is out of range, the connection is still rejected. An explicit RemoteVersionRange such as ^1.0.0 would allow minor skew.
verdicts.note: All five SML quotes and the docs quote are verbatim. SMLNetworkManager.cpp, ModLoadingLibrary.cpp and SemVersion.cpp are byte-identical at the pin and on master (the pin is master HEAD). SML LICENSE.txt at the pin is byte-identical to the canonical GPLv3 text apart from the trailing newline, so there is no exception. GitHub reports GPL-3.0. 193 files under Mods/SML/Source have no license header (the only grep hits were 'FGPlayerController'); README and CREDITS have no license text. All 3 FAQ quotes and both license-list quotes (#Expat, #apache2) are verbatim in the right sections. FicsIt-Networks (Panakotta00/FicsIt-Networks) is GPL-3.0 per the GitHub API. FRM (porisius) has no license in the API and no LICENSE file in the root tree. Circuitry on SMR has an empty source_url and no license text on its page, which is weak evidence. 'No court has settled it for SML' is an absence claim, so unverifiable. Add: FAQ #GPLPluginsInNF says a GPL plug-in combined with a nonfree main program (FactoryGame) conflicts unless an exception is added, and the more direct entry #IfLibraryIsGPL says the whole combination must be GPL or GPL-compatible, which favours MIT or Apache-2.0 for a mod. FSF position only, not legal advice.
